area: Client-side block placement prediction on Minecraft 26.2 (Mojang official mappings): where a block lands (BlockPlaceContext) and whether placement would succeed (BlockItem/BlockState/CollisionGetter legality chain)

Body: return this.replaceClicked; — the field, computed once in the ctor. Stale if the world changes after construction.

Different semantics: getClickedPos() never offsets (always the hit pos), canPlace() = level.getBlockState(hitPos).canBeReplaced(this), isSecondaryUseActive()=false, getRotation()=0. Use it only for dispenser-style placement, not to emulate a player.

PUBLIC but MUTATING — do not use as a probe. On a ClientLevel it really sets the block and really shrinks the client stack.

Only BlockItem declares this method (scanned all of net.minecraft.world.item).

PROTECTED, returns true. Overridden to false only by net.minecraft.world.item.ScaffoldingBlockItem (verified by scanning the package for the symbol). You cannot read it from client code.
PUBLIC and @Nullable (returns the context unchanged by default). Overridden by ScaffoldingBlockItem. Call it before getStateForPlacement if you want to match vanilla exactly.
public.

ANSWER to Q5 (no-entity-in-the-way half). Body: VoxelShape shape = state.getCollisionShape(this, pos, context); return shape.isEmpty() || this.isUnobstructed(null, shape.move(pos)); Callable on a Level/ClientLevel reference.
STUB — body is literally `return true;`. On a bare CollisionGetter the entity check is a no-op.

The REAL implementation: iterates getEntities(source, shape.bounds()) and returns false for any !isRemoved() && entity.blocksBuilding entity whose bounding box intersects the shape (skipping passengers of the same vehicle).

gotchas: The (Level, Player, InteractionHand, ItemStack, BlockHitResult) ctor is PROTECTED on both UseOnContext and BlockPlaceContext on 26.2. A client can absolutely build a BlockPlaceContext with no server — but through `new BlockPlaceContext(Player, InteractionHand, ItemStack, BlockHitResult)`, which derives the level from `player.level()`. You therefore CANNOT inject a Level different from player.level(); a caller that assumed the 5-arg ctor was public will not compile. The only public ctor that takes an explicit Level is DirectionalPlaceContext, and it forces player=null plus dispenser semantics.

BlockPlaceContext.canPlace() is NOT a placement-legality check, despite the name. Its body is `replaceClicked || level.getBlockState(getClickedPos()).canBeReplaced(this)` — pure replaceability of the target position. It knows nothing about block survival, entities in the way, reach, adventure mode, or the world border. Treating canPlace() as 'placement succeeds' will report true for a stone block placed inside a standing mob.

The real legality decision lives in `BlockItem.canPlace(BlockPlaceContext, BlockState)` and it is PROTECTED — uncallable from client code. Every symbol inside its body is public, so replicate it verbatim: `(!mustSurvive() || state.canSurvive(level, pos)) && level.isUnobstructed(state, pos, CollisionContext.placementContext(player))`. `mustSurvive()` is also protected (true by default, false only for ScaffoldingBlockItem), so client code has to hardcode `true` and will wrongly reject scaffolding.

BlockItem.place(BlockPlaceContext) is public but MUTATES: placeBlock does `level.setBlock(pos, state, 11)` and place() then fires playSound, gameEvent and `itemStack.consume(1, player)`. On a ClientLevel that creates a real local ghost block and really shrinks the client's stack. Never call it as a 'would this work' probe. Vanilla only calls it (via ItemStack.useOn) inside MultiPlayerGameMode.startPrediction, which is private, so the change can be rolled back on server ack.

Level.mayInteract(Entity, BlockPos) returns `true` unconditionally on the base Level class — ServerLevel overrides it for spawn protection. So a client-side prediction structurally cannot see spawn protection, and there is no client-visible substitute. Same blind spot for the server's own reach/anticheat in ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.

`Block.canSurvive` does not exist on 26.2. javap on net.minecraft.world.level.block.Block shows no canSurvive declaration at all; it only inherits `protected boolean canSurvive(BlockState, LevelReader, BlockPos)` from BlockBehaviour. The one public entry point is `BlockState.canSurvive(LevelReader, BlockPos)` on BlockBehaviour$BlockStateBase.

CollisionGetter.isUnobstructed(Entity, VoxelShape) is a stub whose body is `return true;`. The genuine entity-overlap logic is EntityGetter.isUnobstructed, wired in by CommonLevelAccessor (bytecode confirms invokespecial to EntityGetter.isUnobstructed). Consequence: `level.isUnobstructed(state, pos, ctx)` on a Level/ClientLevel does the real check, but the same call against a plain CollisionGetter reference (a chunk view, a snapshot wrapper) silently passes every entity test.

26.2 wants `CollisionContext.placementContext(@Nullable Player)` here, not `of(player)` or `empty()`. placementContext sets placement=true so CollisionContext.isPlacement() is true; the other factories leave it false, which can yield a different collision shape for placement-sensitive blocks and make your prediction disagree with vanilla.

BlockState.canBeReplaced has three overloads on 26.2 and only one is the placement one. `canBeReplaced(BlockPlaceContext)` is placement; `canBeReplaced(Fluid)` is fluid flow; the no-arg `canBeReplaced()` just returns the `replaceable` Properties flag. The default BlockBehaviour body for the placement overload is `state.canBeReplaced() && (ctx.getItemInHand().isEmpty() || !ctx.getItemInHand().is(this.asItem()))` — the same-item clause means a replaceable block refuses to be replaced by its own item.

`replaceClicked` (and therefore getClickedPos() and replacingClickedOnBlock()) is computed once inside the constructor, before your code runs. Cache a BlockPlaceContext across a world change and it silently reports the old target position. Rebuild it every tick / after every setBlock.

getNearestLookingDirection(), getNearestLookingVerticalDirection() and getNearestLookingDirections() on BlockPlaceContext dereference getPlayer() with no null guard (Direction.orderedByNearest(Entity) reads entity.getViewXRot immediately). getPlayer() is @Nullable, and DirectionalPlaceContext is the only subclass that overrides them — so calling them on a player-less context NPEs.
UseOnContext.getHitResult() is `protected final`, so once you hand a BlockHitResult to a context you cannot read it back out. Keep your own reference if you need hit.getDirection() later.

BlockItem.getPlacementState is protected and is overridden by GameMasterBlockItem and StandingAndWallBlockItem; updatePlacementContext (public, @Nullable) is overridden by ScaffoldingBlockItem. For those items, calling only the public `Block.getStateForPlacement(ctx)` gives a state vanilla would not have placed. For a plain full-cube block the default path (defaultBlockState()) is exact.

Level.getWorldBorder() is not declared on Level — it comes from CollisionGetter as an abstract method and is implemented on ClientLevel. It compiles fine off a Level-typed reference, but reflection/AT work keyed to `Level.getWorldBorder` will not find it.
